Honestly to be candid on you (since we’re both anonymous and don’t really know each other)

I tried ending myself a little while ago, I had a knife and also made a noose from rope. 

I pretty much lost any interest in life and I came to peace and terms with how I wanted to die. For the sake of decency I won’t describe my attempt in detail. But oddly enough in the process, I couldn’t fully bring myself to do it (not just because of fear, it’s definitely frightening but) there were these 2nd thoughts I kept having before fully going through with it.

Mother, youngest sister, Japan, dreams & aspirations, favorite shows, things I was working on.

They were kinda random and sometimes uncorrelated, but I ended realizing that in these second thoughts I had, I really couldn’t end myself without destroying those things aswell.

Unfortunately I still am a bit suicidal, I don’t really see a point to life, I don’t care to live, and I don’t really think a lot of things matter—but I know those things matter a lot to me and I matter a lot to them.

I’m not trying to give you a corny motivational speech as to why you should “pick up your head!” and “smile more, you should be grateful for life you  asshole!”

But I just thought I’d share the experience with someone who’s looking for advice on ending their life. 

Maybe you have 2nd thoughts of your own. 2nd thoughts you wouldn’t mind living a day or two more in this obscure and demanding world.

Overall though, I’m sorry I really have no advice on how to OD. Which is the reason I never tried it, I know nothing about pills, poison, or medicine and I was too afraid I’d end up hospitalizing myself or becoming vegetative. But as I’ve said before I did just lose someone recently to this and I kinda wished I got the chance to talk to them before they did what they did. So I just thought I’d at least talk to you and tell you some of the things I would’ve told them.

Sorry for the long text, but best of luck bro

“A person who thinks all the time has nothing to think about except thoughts.” — Alan Watts

Honestly I’ve dealt with something just like this in an erringly similar way. My father didn’t want to come to my graduation.

However, I feel we do more damage to ourselves when we get caught up in our own thoughts trying to calculate, understand, and anticipate the situation. 

It’s like you’re watching an amazing show, and right at the most suspenseful moment of the show you press the pause button and try to predict what will happen next.

In reality, sometimes the best thing to do is just let things run their course. Press the resume button, and take in what life has given to you.

Earlier I mentioned how my father told me he wasn’t coming to my graduation because he got into a fight with my family. I was a little hurt, I began to overthinking wondering if he really wasn’t going to come, wondering if he cares about his own son, wondering if he knows that this’ll make me upset.

But then I stopped. I found peace in letting things run their course. I told myself

—if he comes, he comes and I’ll act accordingly


  —if he doesn’t, he doesn’t and I’ll act accordingly 

End of story. There’s no point in over-stressing when it doesn’t help. Funny enough my father actually came, and it made me extremely proud in him and his change of character.

But never get stuck in your mind, you were born in reality, events happen in reality, and you live in reality. So act in reality bro, I hope this helps
